newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL SEEK CONSISTENCY AND PLACE IN HISTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL SEEK CONSISTENCY AND PLACE IN HISTORY.

text.p: Liverpool will want to prove they can establish a lead and hold on to it when they face Norwegian outsiders Brann Bergen in the Cup Winners' Cup on Thursday night.

The four-times European champions are clear favourites to win the quarter-final second-leg tie at Anfield after their 1-1 draw in the first leg but manager Roy Evans must be alarmed at the way his side have squandered leads and conceded late goals in their last three matches.
In Norway two weeks ago, Robbie Fowler gave Liverpool a lead inside the first 10 minutes only for Brann to pull back a goal after the break.
Four days later the Merseysiders saw a three-goal lead against Newcastle evaporate within minutes and needed an injury-time strike from Fowler for a 4-3 victory.
Fowler put them in front in their last league match, against Nottingham Forest, but again they caved in and had to settle for a 1-1 draw.
While they continue to show such inconsistency, Liverpool's hopes of making history by lifting the one European trophy to have so far eluded them appear doomed to failure.
If they do win the Cup Winners' Cup they will become the first English club in an elite group -- along with Juventus, Barcelona, Ajax and Bayern Munich -- to have won all three European trophies.
Few doubt they have the ability to beat Brann comprehensively but at the back of Evans's mind on Thursday night will be the memory of Liverpool's Scandinavian debacle last season.
Then, they drew against Brondby in Denmark in the first leg of a UEFA Cup tie and were widely expected to sweep them aside in the return match.
But Brondby walked away from Anfield with a 1-0 victory to dump Liverpool out of a Europe they once ruled.
Former England international Mark Wright is expected to return to the heart of the Liverpool defence after missing the first leg with a groin strain.
He will replace Steve Harkness and will be given the job of subduing Brann's highly-rated striker Tore Andre Flo.

The Norwegians come to England with order restored in their camp after two of their top players, midfielder Jan Ove Pedersen and goalkeeper Birkir Kristinsson, decided not to take the club to court over an administrative error which meant they missed the first leg and will not play on Thursday.
Brann forgot to register the two men after they returned from spells on loan.
Pedersen and Kristinsson threatened the club with court action, claiming compensation totalling 160,000 pounds ($255,000), but they backed down this week in the face of an outcry from Brann's fans.
Liverpool - David James, Neil Ruddock, Mark Wright, Dominic Matteo, Stig Inge Bjornebye, Jason McAteer, Jamie Redknapp, Patrick Berger, John Barnes, Steve McManaman, Robbie Fowler.
Brann Bergen - Vidar Bahus, Stefan Paldan, Per-Ove Ludvigsen, Claus Eftevaag, Morten Pedersen Eirik Skjalaaen, Roger Helland, Arne Vidar Moen, Geir Hasund, Tore Andre Flo, Agust Gylfason.
